newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: RUSSIA TO RESUME PAYING CZECH DEBT-MINISTER QUOTED.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA TO RESUME PAYING CZECH DEBT-MINISTER QUOTED.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik agreed with Russian officials on a payment schedule for billions of dollars in debt Moscow owes the Czech Republic, the CTK news agency reported on Friday.

It quoted Kocarnik on his return from a working visit to Russia as saying that Moscow would begin repaying its debt to the Czech Republic with yearly payments of $190 million, of which $126 million was interest on the debt.
Further details were not immediately available.
The Czechs and the Russians have been arguing for years over money Moscow owes Prague on loans granted to the former Soviet Union.
Russia's non-payment on the credit in 1996 was a contributing factor to the 1.6 billion crown Czech state budget deficit.

In mid-1994, Russia agreed to pay the debt back at an exchange rate of one dollar to the rouble, meaning the outstanding debt totalled $3.5 billion, $330 million of which was owed to former Czech state businesses.
A schedule was set up in 1994 enabling Russia to pay back the debt in various instalments through 2003 but Moscow suspended payments in 1996.
